collections.title: Autumn 2026 Mathematics Mock
collections.description: 12 original, equally weighted written problems. Based on available autumn 2026 lecture and exercise sheets, with broader review from the May 2026 paper and autumn reference. Mark your written work with the worked solutions after submission.

questions.title: Simplify an algebraic fraction
questions.promptMarkdown: Simplify $\frac{6x^2-24}{3(x-2)}$ and state any excluded value.
hints: Factor the numerator before cancelling.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $6x^2-24=6(x-2)(x+2)$, so the expression simplifies to $2(x+2)$ for $x\ne 2$. The original denominator is zero at $x=2$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 1. Basic algebra and mathematical language

rubricChecks: Simplify to $2(x+2)$
Exclude $x=2$

questions.title: Compare growth over two years
questions.promptMarkdown: A balance of 5,000 NOK grows by 8% in year 1 and falls by 5% in year 2. Find the final balance in NOK.
hints: Multiply the two growth factors.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $5000(1.08)(0.95)=5130$ NOK. The overall growth factor is $1.026$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 2. Rates of change, powers, roots and interest

questions.title: Compare two projects at 10%
questions.promptMarkdown: Project A costs 900 now and pays 550 at the end of each of years 1 and 2. Project B costs 900 now and pays 1,150 at the end of year 2 only. At a 10% annual discount rate, which has the higher NPV? Show both NPVs.
hints: Both initial costs are already at time zero. Discount each later payment separately.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 3. Present value, cash flows and internal rate of return

rubricChecks: Discount payments at their own dates
Compare the correct NPVs and choose A

questions.title: Value a savings annuity
questions.promptMarkdown: You deposit 1,000 NOK at the end of each of four years. The account earns 5% annually. How much is in the account just after the fourth deposit? Give NOK to two decimals.
hints: The first deposit earns three years of interest, and the fourth earns none.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 4. Geometric series, annuities and continuous compounding

questions.title: Find two roots by substitution
questions.promptMarkdown: Solve $x^4-13x^2+36=0$ over the reals.
hints: Let $u=x^2$ and factor the resulting quadratic.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $u^2-13u+36=(u-4)(u-9)$, so $u=4$ or $9$. Taking both signs gives $x=-3,-2,2,3$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 5. Linear and quadratic equations, substitutions and parameters

rubricChecks: Solve for $u=4,9$
Give all four real roots

questions.title: Use the factor theorem
questions.promptMarkdown: Find $a$ if $x-2$ is a factor of $p(x)=x^3+ax^2-5x+6$.
hints: If $x-2$ is a factor, what is $p(2)$?
questions.solutionMarkdown: $p(2)=8+4a-10+6=4+4a$. Setting this equal to zero gives $a=-1$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 6. Polynomials, division and factorisation

questions.title: Check for an extraneous root
questions.promptMarkdown: Solve $\sqrt{x+6}=x$ over the reals. Explain why any rejected root fails.
hints: The right side must be nonnegative before squaring.
questions.solutionMarkdown: Squaring gives $x^2-x-6=0$, so $x=3$ or $-2$. Only $3$ meets $x\ge0$ and $\sqrt{3+6}=3$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 7. Rational equations, radical equations and inequalities

rubricChecks: State $x\ge0$
Reject $-2$ and verify $3$

questions.title: Read the centre of an ellipse
questions.promptMarkdown: Rewrite $4x^2+9y^2-16x+18y-11=0$ in standard ellipse form. Give its centre and semi-axis lengths.
hints: Group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete each square.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $4(x-2)^2+9(y+1)^2=36$, so $\frac{(x-2)^2}{9}+\frac{(y+1)^2}{4}=1$. The centre is $(2,-1)$ and the horizontal and vertical semi-axis lengths are $3$ and $2$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 8. Functions, lines, quadratics, circles and ellipses

rubricChecks: Obtain the standard form
Identify the centre and both semi-axis lengths

questions.title: Distinguish a hole from an asymptote
questions.promptMarkdown: Find the hole and vertical asymptote of $f(x)=\frac{(x-1)(x+3)}{(x-1)(x-2)}$. Give the coordinates of the hole.
hints: Identify the zeros of the original denominator, then cancel the common factor.
questions.solutionMarkdown: The reduced function is $(x+3)/(x-2)$. At $x=1$ it approaches $-4$, so the hole is $(1,-4)$. At $x=2$ the nonzero numerator and zero denominator give a vertical asymptote.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 9. Rational functions, limits, continuity and asymptotes

rubricChecks: Give the hole $(1,-4)$
Give the asymptote $x=2$

questions.title: Find a logarithmic inverse
questions.promptMarkdown: Find $f^{-1}$ for $f(x)=2e^{3x}-4$. State the domain of the inverse.
hints: Solve $y+4=2e^{3x}$ for $x$.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $f^{-1}(x)=\frac13\ln\left(\frac{x+4}{2}\right)$, with domain $x>-4$, the range of $f$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 10. Inverse functions, exponentials and logarithms

rubricChecks: Isolate the exponential and apply the log
State the correct domain

questions.title: Find the tangent slope
questions.promptMarkdown: Find the slope of the tangent to $f(x)=x^2e^x$ at $x=1$. Give a decimal to three places.
hints: Use the product rule before substituting.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $f\prime(x)=2xe^x+x^2e^x$. At $1$ the slope is $3e\approx8.155$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 11. Tangents and differentiation rules

questions.title: Maximise area with a constraint
questions.promptMarkdown: A rectangular garden borders a long straight wall. You have 48 m of fencing for the three other sides. What is the largest garden area in square metres?
hints: If the two shorter fenced sides each have length $x$, the remaining side is $48-2x$.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $A(x)=x(48-2x)$ for $0\le x\le24$. The vertex occurs at $x=12$ and gives $A=288$ square metres. The endpoints give zero.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 12. Stationary points and optimisation in one variable

questions.title: Differentiate an implicit curve
questions.promptMarkdown: Find $dy/dx$ at $(2,1)$ on $x^2+xy+y^2=7$. Give a decimal to two places.
hints: Differentiate $xy$ with the product rule, treating $y$ as a function of $x$.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $2x+y+x y\prime+2y y\prime=0$. Thus $y\prime=-(2x+y)/(x+2y)$, which at $(2,1)$ is $-5/4=-1.25$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 13. Implicit differentiation

questions.title: Locate an inflection point
questions.promptMarkdown: Find the inflection point of $f(x)=x^3-9x^2+5x+4$ and say where the graph is concave down or up.
hints: Look for a sign change in $f\prime\prime(x)$.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $f\prime\prime(x)=6x-18$, which is negative for $x<3$ and positive for $x>3$. As $f(3)=-35$, the inflection point is $(3,-35)$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 14. Second derivatives, convexity and inflection points

rubricChecks: Check both signs of the second derivative
Give the point $(3,-35)$

questions.title: Evaluate a zero-over-zero limit
questions.promptMarkdown: Evaluate $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{e^{2x}-1-2x}{x^2}$ using L’Hôpital’s rule.
hints: After the first differentiation, check whether the limit is still of the indeterminate form $0/0$.
questions.solutionMarkdown: The first derivative ratio is $(2e^{2x}-2)/(2x)$, still $0/0$. Differentiating again gives $4e^{2x}/2$, which tends to $2$.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 15. Limits with L'Hôpital's rule

questions.title: Minimise average cost
questions.promptMarkdown: For output $q>0$, total cost is $C(q)=200+8q+2q^2$. Find the output $q$ that minimises average cost.
hints: Divide total cost by output before differentiating.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $AC=200/q+8+2q$. Setting $AC\prime=-200/q^2+2=0$ gives $q=10$. The derivative changes from negative to positive there.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 16. Marginal cost, revenue and cost optimum

questions.title: Classify demand elasticity
questions.promptMarkdown: Demand is $q(p)=240-4p$ for $0<p<60$. Compute the signed point price elasticity $q\prime(p)p/q(p)$ at $p=40$. Is demand elastic or inelastic there?
hints: Use the quantity at the given price, and compare the absolute value of elasticity with 1.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $q(40)=80$ and $q\prime=-4$, so elasticity is $-4(40)/80=-2$. Its absolute value exceeds 1, so demand is elastic.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 17. Price elasticity

rubricChecks: Calculate the signed elasticity $-2$
Classify demand as elastic

questions.title: Approximate a square root
questions.promptMarkdown: Use the degree two Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ around $x=4$ to approximate $\sqrt{4.4}$. Give four decimal places.
hints: $f\prime(4)=1/4$ and $f\prime\prime(4)=-1/32$. Include the $2!$ in the quadratic term.

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 18. Linearisation and Taylor polynomials

questions.title: Problem 1 · Combine derivative rules
questions.promptMarkdown: Differentiate each function. Give the domain where each derivative exists. (a) $\sqrt{4+x^2}$, (b) $(x-1)e^{2x}$, (c) $\ln(x)/x$.
questions.contextMarkdown: Allow 180 minutes for this mock. All 12 problems carry equal weight. Show your reasoning, then compare your work with the marking checklist after submission.
hints: For each part, identify the outermost operation before differentiating.
questions.solutionMarkdown: (a) Chain rule gives $x/\sqrt{4+x^2}$ for every real $x$. (b) Product and chain rules give $e^{2x}(2x-1)$ for every real $x$. (c) Quotient rule gives $(1-\ln x)/x^2$ for $x>0$.
rubricChecks: Correct chain-rule derivative and domain
Correct product-rule derivative and domain
Correct quotient-rule derivative and domain

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 11. Tangents and differentiation rules

questions.title: Problem 2 · Apply the mean value theorem
questions.promptMarkdown: For $f(x)=x^3-3x^2+x$ on $[0,3]$, compute the secant slope. Verify that the mean value theorem applies and find every point in $(0,3)$ where the tangent is parallel to the secant.
hints: The endpoints define the secant, but the theorem asks for an interior point.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $f(0)=0$ and $f(3)=3$, so the secant slope is $1$. A polynomial is continuous on the closed interval and differentiable on its interior. Solve $f\prime(c)=3c^2-6c+1=1$, giving $c=0$ or $2$. Only $c=2$ lies in $(0,3)$.
rubricChecks: Compute the secant slope and check both hypotheses
Identify $c=2$ and exclude the endpoint

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 11. Tangents and differentiation rules

questions.title: Problem 3 · Find an implicit tangent
questions.promptMarkdown: The curve is given by $x^2+xy+2y^2=8$. Verify that $(2,1)$ lies on the curve, derive $dy/dx$, and find the tangent line at $(2,1)$.
hints: Differentiate $xy$ and $y^2$ with $y$ treated as a function of $x$.
questions.solutionMarkdown: At $(2,1)$ the left side is $4+2+2=8$. Differentiating gives $2x+y+(x+4y)y\prime=0$, so $y\prime=-(2x+y)/(x+4y)$ when $x+4y\ne0$. The slope at $(2,1)$ is $-5/6$ and the tangent is $y-1=-\frac56(x-2)$.
rubricChecks: Verify the point and differentiate correctly
Give the correct slope and tangent equation

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 13. Implicit differentiation

questions.title: Problem 4 · Distinguish a stationary inflection from a minimum
questions.promptMarkdown: Let $f(x)=x^4-4x^3$. Find and classify its stationary points. State where it is concave up and concave down, and give both inflection points.
hints: A zero derivative tells you where to check. Use sign changes to decide what happens there.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $f\prime=4x^2(x-3)$ is negative on both sides of $0$ and becomes positive at $3$. The minimum is $(3,-27)$ and $0$ is stationary without being an extremum. $f\prime\prime=12x(x-2)$ is positive for $x<0$ and $x>2$, negative for $0<x<2$. The inflection points are $(0,0)$ and $(2,-16)$.
rubricChecks: Classify the two stationary points from the first derivative
Give the curvature intervals and verify both inflection points

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 14. Second derivatives, convexity and inflection points

questions.title: Problem 5 · Solve a logarithmic inequality
questions.promptMarkdown: (a) Simplify $\frac{6x^2-6}{9x+9}$ and state the excluded value. (b) Solve $\ln(x-1)+\ln(x+3)\ge\ln(12)$. Justify the domain and endpoints in part (b).
hints: For (a), factor the numerator and denominator. For (b), check both log arguments before combining the logarithms.
questions.solutionMarkdown: (a) The numerator is $6(x+1)(x-1)$ and the denominator is $9(x+1)$. The expression is $2(x-1)/3$ for $x\ne-1$. (b) Both arguments are positive when $x>1$. On this domain, monotonicity of logarithms gives $(x-1)(x+3)\ge12$. Thus $(x+5)(x-3)\ge0$, which reduces to $x\ge3$. At $x=3$ equality holds and both logs exist.
rubricChecks: Simplify the fraction and preserve the excluded value
Set the correct log domain and remove the logs correctly
Solve the inequality and include $x=3$

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 7. Rational equations, radical equations and inequalities

questions.title: Problem 6 · Factor a polynomial and read its sign
questions.promptMarkdown: For $p(x)=x^3-2x^2-5x+6$, show that $x-1$ is a factor. Factor $p$ fully and solve $p(x)\le0$.
hints: Evaluate the polynomial at 1, then divide and use a sign chart.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $p(1)=0$. Dividing by $x-1$ gives $x^2-x-6=(x-3)(x+2)$. All roots are simple, so the signs on the four intervals cut by $-2,1,3$ are respectively $-,+,-,+$. The solution is $(-\infty,-2]\cup[1,3]$.
rubricChecks: Verify the factor and obtain the full factorisation
Use correct interval signs and include all three roots

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 6. Polynomials, division and factorisation

questions.title: Problem 7 · Sketch a rational function with a hole
questions.promptMarkdown: For $f(x)=(2x^2-3x-5)/(x^2-x-2)$, find the domain, any hole, and both asymptotes. Sketch the graph or describe which side of the horizontal asymptote each branch lies on.
hints: Factor both polynomials and preserve the restrictions from the original denominator.
questions.solutionMarkdown: The factors give $f(x)=(x+1)(2x-5)/((x+1)(x-2))=2-1/(x-2)$ for $x\ne-1,2$. The hole is $(-1,7/3)$, the vertical asymptote is $x=2$, and the horizontal asymptote is $y=2$. The left branch lies above $2$ and the right branch below it.
rubricChecks: Correct domain and hole coordinates
Correct asymptotes and branch positions

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 9. Rational functions, limits, continuity and asymptotes

questions.title: Problem 8 · Value delayed payments and decide whether to invest
questions.promptMarkdown: A renovation costs 18,500 NOK today and pays 8,000 NOK at the end of years 3, 4 and 5. At an effective annual discount rate of 5%, find the present value and NPV. Find the highest price today that would still give a nonnegative NPV.
hints: Draw the cash-flow timeline and discount the first receipt for three years.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $PV=8000(1.05^{-3}+1.05^{-4}+1.05^{-5})\approx19760.53$ NOK. Subtract the cost at time zero to get $NPV\approx1260.53$ NOK. The maximum price is the present value, about 19,760.53 NOK.
rubricChecks: Place and discount the three payments correctly
Compute NPV and identify the break-even price

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 4. Geometric series, annuities and continuous compounding

questions.title: Problem 9 · Compare profit maximisation and cost efficiency
questions.promptMarkdown: A firm faces $p(q)=120-2q$ for $0\le q\le60$ and total cost $C(q)=100+20q+q^2$. For positive output, find the quantity that minimises average cost. For $0\le q\le60$, find the quantity that maximises profit. Explain why the quantities differ.
hints: Write average cost as $C(q)/q$ and profit as $q p(q)-C(q)$.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $AC=100/q+20+q$ has $AC\prime=1-100/q^2$, negative before $q=10$ and positive after. Profit is $\pi=100q-3q^2-100$, a concave parabola with maximum at $q=50/3$. Minimising cost per unit compares marginal with average cost. Maximising profit compares marginal revenue with marginal cost.
rubricChecks: Find and verify the average-cost minimum
Find and verify the profit maximum and explain the two criteria

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 16. Marginal cost, revenue and cost optimum

questions.title: Problem 10 · Connect elasticity with revenue
questions.promptMarkdown: For $p>0$, demand is $D(p)=180/(p+3)^2$. Find the signed price elasticity, the elastic price region, and the price that maximises revenue. Justify the maximum.
hints: Use $E=pD\prime/D$ and relate $1+E$ to the sign of the revenue derivative.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $E=-2p/(p+3)$, so $|E|>1$ exactly when $p>3$. For $R=pD(p)$, $R\prime=D(p)(1+E)=180(3-p)/(p+3)^3$. Revenue increases up to $p=3$ and decreases after, giving a global maximum at $3$.
rubricChecks: Derive the signed elasticity and elastic price region
Use the revenue derivative sign to justify the maximum

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 17. Price elasticity

questions.title: Problem 11 · Invert a function with a restricted range
questions.promptMarkdown: For $f(x)=5-2\sqrt{x+1}$ with $x\ge-1$, find its inverse and state the inverse domain and range. Find the inverse slope at input $1$.
hints: Before squaring, determine the sign of $5-y$ from the original equation.
questions.solutionMarkdown: The function is strictly decreasing with range $(-\infty,5]$. From $\sqrt{x+1}=(5-y)/2$, obtain $f^{-1}(y)=(5-y)^2/4-1$, for $y\le5$, with range $[-1,\infty)$. The derivative of the inverse is $(y-5)/2$, giving $-2$ at $y=1$.
rubricChecks: Find the inverse and its domain and range
Calculate the inverse slope at the stated input

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 10. Inverse functions, exponentials and logarithms

questions.title: Problem 12 · Connect a Taylor approximation to a limit
questions.promptMarkdown: Find the degree-two Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\ln(1+2x)$ at $0$ and use it to approximate $\ln(1.1)$. Then evaluate $\lim_{x\to0}(\ln(1+2x)-2x)/x^2$.
hints: The coefficient on $x^2$ is half the second derivative at zero.
questions.solutionMarkdown: $f(0)=0$, $f\prime(0)=2$, and $f\prime\prime(0)=-4$, giving $T_2=2x-2x^2$. At $x=0.05$ this gives $0.095$. Taylor's remainder is $o(x^2)$, so the requested ratio tends to $-2$. Alternatively, differentiating numerator and denominator twice gives $-4/(1+2x)^2$ divided by $2$, with the same limit.
rubricChecks: Derive the Taylor polynomial and give the approximation
Justify the limit by the remainder or a valid application of L’Hôpital’s rule

obsidianLink.file: math-reference/Mathematics for Data Science - Semester Reference.md
obsidianLink.heading: 18. Linearisation and Taylor polynomials
